questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was very confusing. The Sorbonne uses a lot of different platforms, and they were not easy to navigate, if you weren't familiar with them already.

questions.answer: Not really any. I had to contact my student coordinator via e-mail to get answers to my questions.

questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: For me, it was alright, but it is kind of expensive. I found an apartment via the website "Paris Attitude", and it worked out perfectly.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: You have to have a Guarantor to rent an apartment in France. You can buy one online, or you can get a parent to be your guarantor, but then you have to send in all of their tax information.

How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was awful! So confusing and it felt archaic compared to the University of Copenhagen.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer:
1. There was a meeting for ERASMUS students in the UFR Langue Francaise and UFR Littérature. I was in the 3rd year in the UFR Langue Francaise. Here they gave us some info, as well as some official paper on which we could write the courses we wanted. There was one paper for each UFR (at this meeting only the Langue Francaise and Littérature). 

2. Go home and fill out the papers. You had to find course info (like days, times and location) yourself online. You had to make sure yourself, that the classes didn't clash. You had to fill out a paper from each UFR where you were taking classes. Since I took one class in UFR Lit and the rest in UFR LF, I had to fill out two papers. You had to write all your info (name, student number, etc.) and then the class names, class code as well as which days you wanted (for some classes there were multiple to choose from. Be aware that each class has a CM part and a TD part. You have to choose one of each. 

3. Get an e-mail with a date and time to show up on campus and hand in your papers. For me it was the 26th of January, and classes started the 29th, so I was getting kinda stressed out. I had to show up to Sorbonne Mère (the on near Panthéon) and find two offices, where the student coordinator would take and check the papers. This took a looong time, and there was a long line, so be patient. 

4. Done! I luckily didn't have any problems afterwards. I had written a list of all my classes, so I knew where to go and when.

Bonus: 
Make sure you classes don't clash.
Make sure they're all in the same location, or if not, that you have time to travel to another campus between classes.
It's not uncommon that a class changes classroom a few weeks into the semester, so make sure you check the Sorbonne e-mail often. You can make it automatically forward to your normal e-mail, which makes it much easier to check it.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: There was the meeting, but I didn't really feel like there was a lot of new information tbh.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the classes I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don't stress too much. It felt very late for me, but it was luckily all fine in the end. If in doubt, send an e-mail to your student coordinator, or ask other exchange students.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Some courses were too easy, some were perfect, and some were wayy too hard. It was a little hard to find the balance. Some of the courses, I felt like I already knew the subject, as I had had similar courses on my second or third semester. Another courses was almost impossible, if you weren't a native French speaker, which was really frustrating.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Kinda the same. I'm not used to having classes in big auditioriums, but that's mostly what I had in Paris. Some of the teachers kept forgetting to use the microphone, which was really annoying, so make sure you sit close to the front of the class.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
UFR LANGUE FRANCAISE
L6LFZ052 - Lexicologie et lexicografie
L6LFZ062 - Francophonie et variétes des accents (I've forgotten the name, as it's very long, but it's something like this)
L6LF26SL - Syntaxe générale
L6LFG073 - Phonie et graphie

UFR LITTÉRATURE
L6LA09FR - L'anglais du cinéma

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
UFR LANGUE FRANCAISE
Lexicologie et lexicografie --> A really good and interesting course, but also really difficult especially in the beginning, where my French was a lot worse. It's about a lot of the nuances of French, which can be really difficult to understand or "get"

Francophonie et variétes des accents --> Almost impossible, if you're not French. Not recommended. On the very first day, the teacher played 30 soundclips of different French accents, and we were supposed to guess them... Not very feasible, when you barely speak Parisian French.

Syntaxe générale --> It was alright. I felt like I already knew the whole course from previous classes, so I didn't feel like I learned that much new stuff. 

Phonie et graphie --> A great course! My favourite this semester. The classes was super small (like 15 people), and the teacher speaks kind of slow, which was great for understanding him. And he's super nice. 

UFR LITTÉRATURE
L'anglais du cinéma --> It was interesting in the beginning, but this teacher really loves talking and repeating himself. The examform was just writing an essay, but he didn't really give an guidance or info about it beforehand, so it was a little annoying.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Not really very unexpected, but I forgot that I would have to pay to go to the laundromat, as there wasn't one in my building.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
Most things were a little cheaper than Denmark, but a lot of things were the same price. 

It's a lot cheaper to buy things at the bakery as well as going out to eat.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I didn't join any clubs, so I can speak about that, but I did do yoga the entire semester for free. You can choose from a list of sports, and you can do it for free once a week. You just have to be quick, because it's super popular!

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Lost in Frenchlation! It has nothing to do with Sorbonne, but it's a movieclub, where they show French movies with English subtitles. It's great, and the prices range from 5 to 8 euros. 

Also the apps Meetup and Alowa. There's a lot of events and social gatherings, where you just have to sign up and go.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Lille, Rouen, Nice, Menton, Provins, Mont Saint-Michel.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: It's really difficult. I never managed to make a French friend at university haha. It's much easier at a pub quiz, a social event or something like that.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Nothing really.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The food culture!

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Be persistant! They're not always the best with information, so don't be afraid to contact them again and dubble-check. 

Be patient. They're kinda slow, but most of the time it works out. 

Enjoy it! Eat lots of croissants.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don't start looking at courses before you get access to Moodle. It's much easier to look there, and the information is actually up to date, unlike a lot of the other websites.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting a lot of amazing people, and feeling myself speaking better and better French.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The language and the system of the Sorbonne.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
